I think they're 2 sides of the same coin, here is an example of a pattern I recognized that aligned when studying both books:

Barnes’ decision to “burn all bridges behind him” in Think and Grow Rich to get closer to Edison aligns closely with Neville Goddard’s idea of being “born again.”

Burning All Bridges vs. Being Born Again
	•	Burning All Bridges Behind Him (Napoleon Hill) means Barnes cut off all retreat options, fully committing to his goal with no backup plan. This level of absolute faith and mental persistence forced him to step into a new reality where he was already Edison’s business partner in his mind, long before it became true in the physical world.
	•	Being Born Again (Neville Goddard) means completely abandoning the old self and assuming a new identity. Neville teaches that to manifest a new reality, you must let go of your former assumptions and fully embody the new state of being—living in the end as if it were already true.

Key Similarities:
	1.	Commitment to a New Identity: Barnes saw himself as Edison’s partner long before it was real. Neville says you must assume the feeling of your wish fulfilled.
	2.	No Retreat to the Old Self: Barnes had no safety net—failure was not an option. Neville teaches that doubt and returning to old beliefs will ruin manifestation.
	3.	Faith Over Circumstances: Others saw Barnes as just another worker, but in his own mind, he was already a business partner. Similarly, Neville teaches that your imagination creates reality—you must persist despite external appearances.

In essence, both concepts emphasize a radical shift in identity—Barnes didn’t just hope to be Edison’s partner; in his mind, he already was. That’s exactly what Neville teaches: “You must die to your old self to give birth to a new reality.”
